title: Auto-Pigeon /healthz response
description: The unauthenticated liveness document every long-lived Auto-Pigeon HTTP service serves at GET /healthz. It carries the component's identity AND its version, which is what lets one monitor probe answer both "is it up" and "is it the build we deployed" in a single cheap request — and is why the stale-version check needs no custom code anywhere. A health check must be cheap and bounded: no database dump, no downstream cascade, no secrets, no paths.

status.description: "ok" when this process is alive and serving. Liveness only — readiness, where a component has a meaningful one distinct from liveness, is /readyz or the component's own existing readiness route.

version.description: The same string /version reports. The monitor compares it to the version the launcher expected, so a component still running an older build fails its check instead of quietly serving one.

instance.description: Optional instance identity, for a component running as more than one process from one build.

$comment: additionalProperties is true here and false on /version, deliberately. /version is a closed identity document. /healthz is where a component reports the one or two facts only it can know about its own readiness — AUB's database, AUB's AUE scheduler — and closing it would mean either a schema change per component or four components with no way to say anything true. What stays forbidden is what the description says: secrets, paths, environment, and anything expensive to compute.
